source_links_enforced_means: The flag asserts a specific, checkable contract and it is worth saying which, because a gate leg read it as broader than it is and was right that the difference matters. It asserts that every MEASURED cell records all five mandated source layers with a date on each check, that a layer recorded as found carries what it yielded and a link resolving to that row's own trial identifier, and that a layer recorded as not available carries a reason and a date. Inside a cascade record the link is stored on the layer entry, which is the shape the enforcing detector defines and the shape every object in this batch uses; that is the contract, not an exemption from it. What the flag did NOT originally cover was the published-benchmark block, which is new here and which holds sourced effect values of its own. Rather than narrow the claim, those rows were brought under the same convention and now carry a tier and a resolvable link like any other sourced cell.
title: SGLT2 inhibitors against placebo in chronic heart failure across the ejection fraction spectrum: the four randomised outcome trials that report cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event as a time-to-first hazard ratio
question: In adults with chronic heart failure, what is the hazard of a first cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event with an SGLT2 inhibitor compared with placebo added to background therapy?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the validator's numeric list. Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every measured input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from and a resolvable link to the layer it was read from. Every cell records all five mandated source layers, with a date on every check, so a layer that held nothing is distinguishable from a layer nobody opened. Derived transforms -- the log point and log standard error of each ratio, and the pooled summary -- are computed here and are not claimed to appear in any source.
_estimand_rule: The measure governs what can be POOLED, not who is eligible -- a distinction this object got wrong once and now keeps in two separate columns of the screening log. This object pools TIME-TO-FIRST-EVENT HAZARD RATIOS and nothing else. The hardest case in this review is a trial whose RECURRENT-EVENT analysis is reported, by its publication and its registry alike, AS A HAZARD RATIO: it is excluded, and its screening row explains at length why no automated check in this repository could have caught it if it had been let in. A hierarchical win ratio, whose direction of benefit is inverted, is excluded for the same family of reason.
single_tier_because: Every cell's PRIMARY source is the open-access primary publication and the tier tag on each cell names that layer. That uniformity is not the absence of a cascade: each cell records all five mandated layers, and on all four cells the two regulator layers and the registry are FOUND and agree. The reason the primary tier is the same everywhere is stated on each cell, and it is not the reason the companion review in this batch gives. There, the publication was the only layer printing both a point and a two-sided interval. Here the regulator layers print both as well, so a higher-ranked layer genuinely did hold every cell. The publication is kept because it is the layer that also fixes the follow-up, the adjudication and the analysis set stored beside each estimate, and assembling a cell from a label's estimate and a paper's context would attribute to one document something built from two. Each cell carries that argument explicitly rather than inheriting it from here.
completeness_statement: FULL BUILD, with a stated boundary on the search. Every randomised trial reached by reconciliation against three published syntheses of this class in heart failure, and by the registry records staged for every trial those syntheses name, is either pooled or in ONE screening log with the criterion it fails and the quantity it reports instead. There is exactly ONE SOURCE list, `screening.records`. The object also holds `screening.excluded`, which is not a second table a reader must reconcile: it is a view COMPUTED from the records at build time, row for row, so it cannot say anything the records do not. What this statement does NOT claim is a systematic database search; none was run, the limitation is recorded in the screening block, and a trial missed by all three syntheses and absent from the staged registry layer would be missed here.

verification_basis.what_verifies_this_object: Two things, and neither is a badge this repository can emit about itself. The first is that the object is the single source of truth and the page is a pure projection of it, so a claim on the page that is not in the object cannot exist. The second is a cross-family adversarial gate: the object is read by two model families with independent file access, from different vendors, each asked to find a defect in the ACTUAL object rather than to approve it.
verification_basis.what_is_not_claimed: No internal check is described as independent verification. A script that reads this object and reports that this object is consistent has confirmed consistency and nothing else, and a badge that cannot fail is worth less than no badge, because it teaches a reader to stop looking. The validator finding no defect is reported as exactly that.
verification_basis.bar: Both families must find no defect in the object. A finding about the validator is not a finding about the object and does not block.

handbook.decision: POOL four trials reporting the same effect measure for the same outcome CONCEPT against the same comparator, producing an AVERAGE ACROSS a documented difference in how two of them define the composite, across two molecules and across the ejection-fraction spectrum
handbook.conformance: Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.3 fix the two axes on which ELIGIBILITY turns -- population and comparator -- and every screening decision names which of them it falls on, which is why the log has a criterion column rather than a verdict column. Section 3.2.4 is what keeps the MEASURE out of that list: it cautions that eligibility resting on which outcomes a study reported invites outcome reporting bias, so the measure is recorded in a separate column as a limit on POOLING. Section 10.9 is the authority for that limit, and it gives the hazard ratio as the effect measure for time-to-event data and sanctions combining log hazard ratios by generic inverse variance; all four trials report a Cox hazard ratio for the time to a first event of their primary composite against placebo, so the measure is shared and nothing is converted. What the pool crosses is documented under 10.10.1 in the uniformity table, and the first row of that table is the one that matters: two trials count an urgent heart failure visit inside the composite and two do not. That difference is not smoothed away, not harmonized and not described as absent. Section 10.10.4 governs the model and the between-study variance estimator; restricted maximum likelihood is used and the comparison of estimators that 10.10.4.4 motivates is RUN rather than asserted, and with this little heterogeneity the estimators agree closely, which is reported as the unremarkable result it is. Section 10.14 is why the leave-one-out analysis is here; unlike the other cardiology pool in this batch it changes nothing, and that is itself the finding.

It is NOT a claim that the contributing trials estimate identical quantities: two of them count a component the other two do not. The dimensions on which they differ are listed in the uniformity table, and the pooled value averages across them.

effect_measure: All four report a Cox hazard ratio for the time to a FIRST event of their primary composite. No conversion is performed and none would be valid: the three trials kept out of this pool are kept out precisely because their headline quantities cannot be turned into this one.
comparator: All four randomised against a matching placebo added to background heart failure therapy. No trial in this pool has an active comparator.
outcome_definition: This is the axis the pool crosses, and it is the most important row in this table. The two empagliflozin trials define their composite as cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure. The two dapagliflozin trials ADD a third component, an urgent heart failure visit, which is an outpatient event the empagliflozin trials do not count. The two that count it do NOT define it identically, and that is why each cell stores its trial's own wording instead of a common paraphrase: the earlier trial specifies a visit resulting in intravenous therapy, while the later one and its label describe a visit requiring treatment for worsening heart failure other than merely an increase in oral diuretics, which is the broader criterion. An earlier version of this row applied the narrower intravenous-therapy wording to both, importing one trial's definition onto the other at the point where a reader meets the pooled number; a gate leg was right to read the cells rather than this sentence. The FDA LABEL records a further difference the registry does not post: in the earlier dapagliflozin trial the cardiovascular-death component INCLUDED deaths of undetermined cause and in the later one it excluded them. That distinction is in the label and in one of the prior syntheses; it is NOT in the European product information, so it is credited to the layer that carries it and not to the regulator layers jointly. Nothing here is harmonized, and where a published synthesis DID harmonize it the reconciliation block says so and gives that synthesis's number beside this one.
ejection_fraction_range: Two trials enrolled at or below an ejection fraction of 40% and two enrolled above it, so the pool spans the ejection-fraction spectrum by design rather than by accident. That is the question this object asks, and it is also why a reader looking for a reduced-ejection-fraction answer should not read the headline as one.
drug: Two trials tested dapagliflozin and two tested empagliflozin, each at 10 mg once daily. The pooled value is a CLASS average and not an estimate for either molecule; nothing in this object identifies one as better than the other and the leave-one-out table is where a reader can see how little the average depends on any one of them.
blinding: All four were double-blind with centrally adjudicated components.
endpoint_rank_within_its_own_trial: This composite is the PRIMARY endpoint of every contributing trial, so the pool inherits none of the multiplicity exposure that a secondary endpoint would carry. That is unusual for this batch and it is the main reason the risk-of-bias domain is not downgraded.
follow_up_length: The medians range from just over a year to well over two, and each trial's own median is stored on its cell. The two dapagliflozin trials are described as event-driven by their own registry records, so for that pair the difference reflects event accrual rather than a differing follow-up intention. Nothing staged for the two empagliflozin trials says the same, and an earlier version of this row generalised it to all four; what can be said of them is only that their medians differ.
analysis_population: Each trial's full analysis set equals its randomised total, on all four.

That is reported with the same caveat this batch applies everywhere rather than as reassurance: with four trials the statistic has little power to detect heterogeneity, and a floor value is consistent both with genuine agreement and with not being able to tell. What supports reading it as agreement here is visible without the statistic -- the four point estimates lie in a narrow band and every interval overlaps every other. sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, plus a comparison of between-study variance estimators
sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.14: sensitivity analyses examine whether overall findings are robust to potentially influential decisions. Section 10.10.4.4 governs the estimator half -- it records that methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better and that restricted maximum likelihood is the RevMan default. Section 10.10.4.5 is about INTERPRETATION with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval, not the variance estimator; it is cited for the interval comparison and not for the estimator comparison.
sensitivity.decision_under_test: Two decisions. First, whether the pooled benefit depends on any single trial. Second, whether it depends on the choice of between-study variance estimator and interval method, which with four studies is not automatically a formality even though it turns out to be one here.
sensitivity.leave_one_out_finding: The pooled benefit depends on no single trial. Every leave-one-out fit keeps the null outside its interval and every one lands close to the full pool. This is the opposite of what the companion reduced-ejection-fraction review in this batch found, where dropping the largest trial removed the benefit, and the contrast is worth stating because the two objects share a template and a reader may assume they share a fragility. They do not.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: Section 10.10.4.4 records that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better and that restricted maximum likelihood is now the default in the Cochrane software, and it is the whole of the authority for running this comparison. Nothing in the Handbook instructs a review to compare variance estimators at a particular number of studies; running it is a choice made under section 10.14. Here it is uninformative, and that is reported rather than dropped: a sensitivity analysis that changes nothing is evidence about the result, and only a lane that ran it can say so.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: Restricted maximum likelihood is kept as the headline estimator with the ordinary interval, because section 10.10.4.4 records it as the Cochrane default and as a better estimator than DerSimonian and Laird. With the between-study variance estimated at zero the choice is close to immaterial here, and keeping the default is therefore not a choice that flatters the result. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is reported beside it, with the floor on its scale factor applied so it can widen and can never come out narrower than the ordinary interval.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: The three variance estimators agree, because there is no between-study variance for them to disagree about, and all three intervals exclude the null. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is wider, as its floor guarantees it can only be, and it excludes the null as well. No method tried here reverses the finding. This is reported as a null sensitivity result and not as corroboration: four ways of computing an interval from the same four numbers agreeing is arithmetic, not independent evidence.

grade.certainty_derivation: start high; no downgrades; total -0 -> high

risk_of_bias.basis_in_sources: Every contributing trial is double-blind, randomised one to one against a matching placebo, prospectively registered, and posts results to its registry; the components of the composite are adjudicated by a central committee in each. This object holds each trial's registry record, its primary publication and two regulator documents, and the effect estimate agrees across all four layers on all four trials, which is a check on reporting rather than on conduct but is the check available. The endpoint pooled here is each trial's own PRIMARY, so none of the selective-reporting exposure that a secondary endpoint carries applies. No trial in this pool stopped early for benefit. Not downgraded.

inconsistency.derived_from: The between-study variance estimated by restricted maximum likelihood, and Q against its degrees of freedom, both stored in the heterogeneity block of this result. Q does not exceed its degrees of freedom, so the Higgins statistic is at its floor and there is no heterogeneity for a downgrade to be about. Section 14.2.2 makes the trigger UNEXPLAINED heterogeneity rather than a value of the Higgins statistic, and it cross-references chapter 10. There is no unexplained heterogeneity to carry: the point estimates lie in a narrow band, every interval overlaps every other, and the dimensions on which the trials genuinely differ -- the composite's definition, the ejection-fraction range, the molecule -- are documented in the uniformity table rather than offered as post-hoc explanations. Not downgraded, and the low statistic is reported with the caveat that with four trials it carries little power to detect heterogeneity.

indirectness.basis_in_sources: Population, intervention and comparator are all direct: adults with chronic heart failure, an SGLT2 inhibitor at its approved heart failure dose, against placebo on top of background therapy, with the outcome measured in the trials themselves and not surrogated. The one candidate for indirectness is the OUTCOME, because two trials count an urgent heart failure visit within the composite and two do not. It is not downgraded, and the reasoning is stated rather than assumed: the extra component is a worsening-heart-failure event of the same clinical kind as the other two, it is the minority of events in both trials that count it, and the regulator layers report those trials' composites decomposed so the size of that minority is visible rather than inferred. A reader who wants the strictly harmonized composite instead has it in the reconciliation block, from syntheses that computed it, and this object does not pretend the two are the same quantity.

imprecision.derived_from: The pooled interval stored in this result, which lies wholly below the null, together with the leave-one-out table, in which every fit keeps the null outside its interval, and the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval, which also excludes it. Section 14.2.2 gives three conditions and this object can check two. The interval excludes the null, which is the first. The second asks whether the interval includes appreciable benefit or harm; the upper bound here sits below the threshold the section offers as a rough guide, so the interval does not straddle a boundary between appreciable and negligible effect. The third, the optimal information size, is declared uncomputable below rather than quietly treated as met. Unlike the other cardiology pool in this batch, the precision here is not a property of one trial: every leave-one-out fit keeps the null outside its interval, and so does the more conservative interval method. Not downgraded.
imprecision.ois_note: The optimal information size is a condition section 14.2.2 makes part of adequate precision and it is NOT computable from what this object holds: it needs an assumed control-arm risk and a target difference that no field here carries. It is therefore UNKNOWN rather than satisfied, and this sentence exists so its absence cannot read as a pass. What can be said is that the pooled evidence carries a large absolute event count across every contributing trial, so the decision not to downgrade does not rest on sparse events.

publication_bias.not_assessable_because: Four studies. The funnel-plot and regression methods for small-study effects are not interpretable much below ten, so no assessment is made and none is implied. What can be said without a test is recorded instead and is not offered as a substitute for one: all four trials were prospectively registered, all four posted results to their registry, all four are held here in four independent document layers that agree, and the field's own null results in adjacent populations are published. Rated not assessable, which downgrades nothing on its own.

grade.what_this_certainty_is_about: It is the certainty of the POOLED class average across four trials of two molecules, spanning the ejection-fraction spectrum. It is not a rating of either molecule on its own and not a rating for any one ejection-fraction band. It is also not a rating of the strictly harmonized composite that the published syntheses in the reconciliation block estimate, because that is a different quantity computed from patient-level or trial-level data this object does not hold. Reading this rating as a verdict on one drug in one population would be a misreading, and the sentence is here because that misreading is the easy one.

SCOPE:measure-governs-POOLING-not-eligib.decision: Only a time-to-first-event hazard ratio enters the POOL. Recurrent-event and total-occurrence analyses and hierarchical win ratios do not, whatever the trial or the registry calls them. That is a limit on what can be COMBINED, and it is deliberately NOT used as a reason to leave a trial out of the review: every screened trial is in the log with the quantity it reports, quoted.
SCOPE:measure-governs-POOLING-not-eligib.conformance: Section 10.9 fixes the hazard ratio as the measure for time-to-event data and generic inverse variance as the way to combine log hazard ratios; it is the whole of the authority for the pooling limit, because a win ratio and a recurrent-event analysis are not log hazard ratios and cannot be entered as though they were. Section 3.2.4 is cited for the OPPOSITE reason and the distinction matters: it cautions AGAINST making eligibility turn on which outcomes a study reported, because that invites outcome reporting bias. An earlier version of this object cited 3.2.4 as authority for treating the measure as an eligibility criterion and was being stricter than the Handbook while claiming the Handbook's support. The object's position is now the one it can actually defend: each screened trial fails an axis the Handbook DOES make eligibility -- population under 3.2.1 -- and each screening row records its measure separately, as the reason its value could not have been pooled even had the population matched. The hardest case is unchanged and is the reason the pooling limit exists at all: one excluded trial's recurrent-event analysis is reported by its journal AND its registry AS A HAZARD RATIO, so the label on the quantity is not the quantity, and no automated check in this repository can tell the two apart.

SCOPE:own-primary-not-harmonized.decision: Each trial contributes its OWN primary composite as that trial defines it. This object does not construct a harmonized endpoint across trials, and it does not import one from a synthesis that did.
SCOPE:own-primary-not-harmonized.conformance: Section 10.10.1 is what distinguishes clinical and methodological DIVERSITY from statistical heterogeneity, which is why the uniformity table sits beside the heterogeneity statistic rather than being replaced by it: the difference in composite definition is a difference in the question each trial answered and no statistic computed from four numbers can see it. It is the first substantive row in that table. The alternative was to import published harmonized cells where they exist and fall back on own-primary cells where they do not, which would put two different quantities in one pool while looking tidier than this does. The syntheses that harmonized properly, from data this object does not hold, are reported beside the pool with their scope intact.

SCOPE:population-is-heart-failure-not-ca.decision: A trial enters only if chronic heart failure was an entry requirement. A cardiovascular or renal outcome trial in which some participants happen to have heart failure does not, even when it reports this review's exact endpoint in this review's exact form.
SCOPE:population-is-heart-failure-not-ca.conformance: Section 3.2.1 fixes the population as a defining criterion. This is the boundary that removes the diabetic kidney-disease trial, and that exclusion is the least comfortable one in this object because the quantity it would contribute is available and correctly shaped. The screening row quotes that value rather than hiding it, so the cost of the boundary is visible to a reader who would draw it elsewhere.

SCOPE:class-average-not-molecule.decision: The pool averages across two molecules and reports a class effect. It does not claim, and must not be read as claiming, an estimate for either drug individually.
SCOPE:class-average-not-molecule.conformance: The molecule is a documented crossed dimension in the uniformity table under section 10.10.1, and the leave-one-out analysis run under section 10.14 is what lets a reader see how little the average moves when any one trial is removed. Both are reported; neither is offered as a subgroup analysis, because this object holds no test for a difference between the molecules and does not imply one.

sglt2_newly_unscreened_2026_08_19.third_state_why: ELIGIBLE_NO_RESULTS_YET is neither eligible-and-assessed nor excluded. sglt2_newly_unscreened_2026_08_19.stronger_ground_rule: Where more than one limb fails, the decision is recorded on the STRONGEST ground and the others are named rather than leaned on. Where STATUS settles a trial, the population question is not argued at all -- deciding a trial on a contestable limb when an uncontestable one is available manufactures a firmer verdict than the evidence supports.

DACAMI. Registered condition 'Anterior MI'. Dapagliflozin vs glucose tablet post-STEMI -- an acute myocardial-infarction population, not chronic heart failure.

EMPATHY, and THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL EXCLUSION IN THIS SET, so the reason is given in full. n=1364, and its primary is 'Time to first event of adjudicated cardiovascular death, or adjudicated hospitalization for heart failure' -- EXACTLY the estimand this object pools, so it would be poolable if it were eligible. It is excluded on POPULATION alone: the registered condition is 'Acute Decompensated Heart Failure', and this review's criterion says CHRONIC. That is a real and narrow distinction, not a technicality -- but it is also the single trial most likely to change this answer if the population limb is ever widened to admit acute decompensation. RECORDED HERE SO THAT DECISION IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN BURIED IN A TALLY.

Steno1. The experimental arm is a MULTIFACTORIAL BUNDLE -- aspirin, semaglutide, sotagliflozin and finerenone together -- against standard intervention. Four agents differ between arms, so no estimate is attributable to the SGLT2 inhibitor. This is the one-arm-only defect that topic_identity.locate() was corrected for (pioglitazone plus dapagliflozin): appearing in the experimental arm is not the same as being the contrast.
SUGARNSALT. Registered as diabetic nephropathy / chronic kidney failure / type 1 diabetes, with eGFR after wash-out as the primary. The randomised population is a renal one.

EMPA-HEART-3. NOT_YET_RECRUITING, n=410. Registered condition is 'Congenital Heart Disease', which would very likely fail the population limb -- but the trial has not started, so there is nothing to assess and no need to decide it on weaker ground.

trials.title: IV Iron and SGLT2 Inhibitor on Ventricular Function and Myocardial Iron Content in Heart Failure With Iron Deficiency

eligibility_limbs_all_reported.POPULATION: HOLDS. conditions = ['Heart Failure, Systolic', 'Iron Deficiencies']; inclusion requires EF <= 40% with iron deficiency, and the exclusions remove acute coronary presentations. Chronic HFrEF.
eligibility_limbs_all_reported.COMPARATOR: HOLDS, and it needs the arms read rather than the drug list. Arm 1 is ferric carboxymaltose + dapagliflozin; arm 2 is ferric carboxymaltose + PLACEBO of dapagliflozin. FCM is in both, so it is background and the randomised contrast between those two arms is dapagliflozin against its placebo on top of background therapy -- exactly this review's comparison. A third arm gives placebo for both.

trials.reason: NOT_YET_RECRUITING, so it has reported nothing. Settled on STATUS, which is the uncontestable ground, and the contestable limbs are not argued.
trials.and_when_it_does_report_it_still_will_no: Recorded now so it is not mistaken for a trial that will change the answer. Its primary is LVEF by cardiac MRI at 30 days and its two secondaries are myocardial iron content and strain by T2* CMR. NO time-to-first-event outcome at ANY rank, so s10.9 will not permit combining it with this object's hazard ratios however it reports. n=99.

trials.title: Dapagliflozin for Cardio-renal Protection After ICU Discharge

eligibility_limbs_all_reported.POPULATION: FAILS. Enrolment is patients READY FOR DISCHARGE FROM ICU after more than 24 hours of mechanical ventilation and/or vasopressors, entering on 'NT-proBNP > 800 ng/L or BNP > 90 ng/L AND/OR eGFR between 25 and 90'. The and/or means a participant can qualify on the RENAL threshold alone with no heart-failure diagnosis at all. This is a post-critical-illness population, not the chronic ambulatory heart failure this review asks about -- the same limb on which this object already excludes SOLOIST-WHF, EMPULSE and eight others.
eligibility_limbs_all_reported.COMPARATOR: HOLDS. 'Drug: One tablet of placebo of dapagliflozin 10 mg'. Its arm typing is ACTIVE_COMPARATOR for the dapagliflozin arm and PLACEBO_COMPARATOR for the placebo arm -- the inversion that made the old classifier call the drug the comparator, and the reason it surfaced here at all.

trials.reason: EXCLUDED ON POPULATION. The registered condition string reads 'Heart Failure and Chronic Kidney Disease Post-ICU', and it is the POST-ICU qualifier that decides it, not the words 'heart failure' inside it. Deciding this from the condition string alone would have admitted it.
trials.what_it_would_have_added_if_the_limb_wer: n=600, PHASE3, RECRUITING, with all-cause mortality and unscheduled hospitalisation for heart failure among its three co-primaries at one year. It is not this object's estimand -- a time-to-first CV-death-or-worsening-HF composite -- so even under a widened population it would enter on the POOLABILITY axis rather than the pool. Stated so a reader can see the cost of the boundary rather than take it on trust.

ceiling.statement: NO RESULT IN THIS REVIEW CAN REACH LOW RISK OF BIAS ON THE EVIDENCE WE CAN REACH, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT OUR ACCESS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TRIALS. The two domains that would distinguish LOW from SOME CONCERNS need documents this review does not hold: D1 needs allocation concealment and baseline data, which are in neither the registration nor the published abstract; D5 needs the trial's statistical analysis plan, which is not held for any trial. SOME CONCERNS IS THEREFORE THE CEILING, NOT A FINDING. A trial rated SOME CONCERNS here may well be at low risk of bias -- we cannot show it, and we do not imply the opposite.
ceiling.what_would_change_it: Retrieving each trial's full published report and its statistical analysis plan or protocol. Until then the rating is bounded by what we read, and the bound is reported rather than the reader inferring it.
ceiling.why_this_is_stated_rather_than_left_impl: A rating of SOME CONCERNS with no explanation reads as a judgement against the trial. Omitting the reason would manufacture a criticism exactly as a low-by-default manufactures a reassurance -- the same defect pointed the other way.

risk_of_bias.THE_SAME_TRIAL_IS_JUDGED_DIFFERENTLY_IN_: DAPA-HF (NCT03036124) contributes to both outcomes on this object. In `threecomp_cvdeath_hhf_urgent` the pooled outcome IS its registered primary and D5 is LOW. In `harmonised_cvdeath_or_hhf` the pooled outcome is the TWO-component composite, which is NOT its registered primary -- its primary carries a third component, an urgent heart-failure visit -- and D5 is SOME_CONCERNS. THAT IS WHY RoB 2 IS ASSESSED PER RESULT AND NOT PER TRIAL, and it is the clearest example of it in this corpus.
risk_of_bias.THE_EMPEROR_TRIALS_DO_NOT_MASK_THEIR_OUT: NCT03057977 and NCT03057951 register masking as DOUBLE -- participant and investigator. Their endpoints are ADJUDICATED, which their registered outcome titles state, but no registration states that the adjudicators were blinded. DAPA-HF and DELIVER are QUADRUPLE-masked and D4 is LOW on both.
risk_of_bias.ONE_ASSESSOR_ONLY: ASSESSED BY ONE ASSESSOR. Under the standing specification that risk of bias 2 must be complete and done by TWO AIs from different model families, THIS ASSESSMENT IS INCOMPLETE. `rob2.assessors` is deliberately NOT written.

superseded_state_2026_08_21._why_this_is_kept: The prior value of `risk_of_bias` held 4 key(s) this assessment does not carry. protocol.why: A protocol specified before data collection is a HISTORICAL FACT ABOUT THE PAST and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them.
protocol.what_was_actually_done: Eligibility criteria were derived POST HOC from the trials and the methodological authority, and the derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility_provenance` with the source of each.
protocol.authority_permitting_it: MECIR R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria PROVIDED THEY ARE DECLARED AS SUCH. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.
protocol.forward_remedy: For topics not yet built, a protocol is to be written and registered BEFORE the search is executed, so that the claim becomes true GOING FORWARD. It is never to be made true retroactively for a built topic.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In adults with chronic heart failure, what is the hazard of a first cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event with an SGLT2 inhibitor compared with placebo added to background therapy?

It pools 4 randomised trials, against placebo added to background heart failure therapy.

The outcomes pooled are Cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio; cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, first event; Cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, or an urgent heart-failure visit, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

what_this_review_does_not_publish_2026_0: WHAT THIS REVIEW DOES NOT PUBLISH. This review also examined one outcome for which no pooled estimate is published: Cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio (k=4) -- The four trials do not share one endpoint. Each of those outcomes is recorded on this review with the reason it was not pooled, and none of them contributes to the estimate reported above (0.7636 at k=3, 0.7835 at k=2). A reader meeting the pooled result should not take it as covering every outcome, or every trial, this review examined. This sentence exists because a second, independent reading -- by a different model family, given the object and the abstract and none of our conclusions -- found that a reader would reasonably conclude the review pools all relevant trials, and that the object does not support that. The withdrawals were already recorded beside the outcomes they concern; they were invisible from the abstract, which is where the impression forms.
